advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Validate (or re-run `_pai_check_config`) on the recovered slot endpoint so a malformed per-class endpoint fails as clearly as a malformed top-level base_url.
evidence: runner.py:307 `_pai_check_config(cfg)` runs on the ORIGINAL cfg, before recovery
runner.py:361-364 `if not cfg.base_url ...: cfg = replace(cfg, base_url=slot_endpoint)` mutates cfg AFTER validation
structured_run.py:686-690 validates scheme/netloc and raises LLMConfigError for a base_url 'not an absolute URL'
model_classes.py:164 `endpoint = raw.get("endpoint")` — slot endpoints are never scheme/host-validated at parse time
advisory.finding: The endpoint recovered from a slot into cfg.base_url (runner.py:364) is never validated for scheme/host: `_pai_check_config(cfg)` runs at runner.py:307 BEFORE the recovery block, and slot endpoints are not validated at parse time. A malformed slot endpoint (e.g. 'localhost:1234' with no scheme) therefore silently becomes cfg.base_url and fails deeper in pydantic-ai rather than with the clear LLMConfigError the top-level REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL path emits — contradicting the comment's claim of behaving 'uniformly with the top-level REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL path'.
scenarios: Operator sets REBAR_LLM_TRIVIAL_ENDPOINT=localhost:1234 (missing http:// scheme) and no top-level base_url

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the regression test to assert the run's provider_provenance records the endpoint host and tier=best_effort, matching the ticket AC.
evidence: test asserts only `out["verdict"] == "PASS"` and `"localhost:1234" in str(stub_openai_server[0].url)` (test lines 369-371)
ticket 6e70 AC: 'provenance base_url is set and tier=best_effort'
runner.py:457-462 provenance_for(base_url=cfg.base_url) and capabilities.py:589 `"tier": "best_effort" if (base_url or via_gateway)` — separately derived, not covered by the routing assertions
advisory.finding: The regression test asserts routing (verdict PASS, 'localhost:1234' in the request URL) but does not assert the ticket's other two named acceptance criteria: that provider provenance records the endpoint base_url/host and that tier flips to best_effort. Those are the invariants the fix's own comment and the ticket AC emphasize, and they are computed from cfg.base_url independently of routing.
scenarios: A future refactor that routes correctly but stops stamping base_url into provenance / stops flipping tier would still pass this test

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test: a slot endpoint present WITH an explicit `cfg.base_url` leaves base_url unchanged (the primary reaches the explicit base_url, not the slot endpoint).
evidence: runner.py:361 `if not cfg.base_url and self._model_override is None:`
Comment at runner.py:360 `# Never overrides an explicit base_url; a class with no slot endpoint is a no-op.`

ABSENCE: only test added is `test_per_class_endpoint_routes_the_primary_through_the_local_builder`, which asserts `cfg.base_url is None` before the run — no case where cfg.base_url is set with a slot endpoint present.
advisory.finding: The new runner guard `if not cfg.base_url` — the documented 'Never overrides an explicit base_url' contract (ticket ACCEPTANCE: 'existing base_url ... behavior unchanged') — is untested. No test configures a slot endpoint AND an explicit `cfg.base_url` and asserts the explicit base_url survives. A regression dropping the `not cfg.base_url` condition would silently clobber an operator's explicit endpoint and go undetected.
scenarios: Operator sets both a top-level base_url and a per-class endpoint; the explicit base_url must win.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test that sets `_configure_class_endpoint(...)` and constructs `_cfg(base_url='http://explicit:9000/v1')`, then asserts the request in `stub_openai_server` went to `explicit:9000`, not `localhost:1234`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a model_override run with a matching slot endpoint does NOT set cfg.base_url from the slot endpoint (endpoint recovery skipped).
evidence: runner.py:361 `if not cfg.base_url and self._model_override is None:`
Diff commit message: 'the offline model_override path is exempt.'
ABSENCE: no test in the added block constructs a PydanticAIRunner with a model_override alongside a configured slot endpoint.
advisory.finding: The `self._model_override is None` guard on the new endpoint-recovery code is untested. The code comment and ticket state the offline model_override (TestModel) path is exempt, but no test exercises an override with a matching slot endpoint to confirm the endpoint is NOT applied. A regression removing that condition would perturb the offline harness path undetected.
scenarios: Offline TestModel harness run for an op whose class slot carries an endpoint.

evidence: model_classes.py:399-400 'Classes are consulted in CLASS_NAMES order, so if two slots name the same primary the first wins.'
ABSENCE: search for `primary_endpoint_for` in tests/ returns no matches (only the runner-level end-to-end test touches it).
advisory.finding: `primary_endpoint_for` has no direct unit test; its documented behaviors — returning None on no match (no-op) and 'first wins' when two CLASS_NAMES slots resolve to the same primary — are only exercised via the single happy-path runner test. The ordering/no-match branches are unverified.
scenarios: Two model-class slots resolve to the same provider:model with different endpoints; the CLASS_NAMES-order winner must be deterministic.
